# Orca plugin host API reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm generate:plugin-schemas` from src/shared/plugins. Do not edit. -->

Host API 1.6 (`"pluginApi": 1`). Workers call a method with `await orca.host.call(name, params)`; panels and custom editors call the same methods through `window.orca.host.call(name, params)`. Each method lists the surfaces allowed to call it; any other surface gets `not_permitted`. `orca.host.has(name)` answers synchronously whether this Orca offers a method on the current surface, and `orca.api` is `{ major, minor }`. See [Plugin authoring](./plugin-authoring.md) for the frame API.

Every call is checked against the capabilities the user approved, and params are validated before Orca runs anything: params are strict, so a field this Orca does not know is refused with `invalid_params` instead of being dropped. Mutations are recorded in the audit log as `plugin:<publisher>.<id>`.

Methods whose capability is `none` need no capability but still need the plugin enabled and approved. `shell.openExternal` and `files.saveAs` also need transient user activation (a click or key press in the calling frame, within a few seconds), are rate-limited, and run only in the desktop app; frames also reach them as `orca.shell.openExternal(url)` and `orca.files.saveAs({ suggestedName, mimeType, data })`, which resolves with `{ status: "saved" }`, or `{ status: "cancelled" }` when the person cancels the dialog. Saved files carry the OS mark for downloaded files.

### `workspace.readContext`

Branch, name and terminal ids of the focused workspace, or null when none is focused.

```ts
(params?: {}) => { branch: string; displayName: string; terminals: { id: string; title?: string }[] } | null
```

### `terminal.sendText`

Types text into one terminal named by id, optionally pressing Enter.

```ts
(params: { terminalId: string; text: string; enter?: boolean }) => { accepted: boolean }
```

### `notifications.show`

Shows a desktop notification.

```ts
(params: { title: string; body?: string }) => { delivered: boolean }
```

### `storage.get`

Reads a JSON value from the plugin's private store; null when absent.

```ts
(params: { key: string }) => { value: JSON }
```

### `storage.set`

Writes a JSON value to the plugin's private store.

```ts
(params: { key: string; value: JSON }) => { ok: true }
```

### `storage.delete`

Removes a key from the plugin's private store.

```ts
(params: { key: string }) => { ok: true }
```

### `storage.keys`

Lists the keys in the plugin's private store.

```ts
(params?: {}) => { keys: string[] }
```

### `secrets.get`

Reads a secret from the plugin's encrypted secrets file; null when absent.

```ts
(params: { key: string }) => { value: string | null }
```

### `secrets.set`

Stores a secret in the plugin's encrypted secrets file.

```ts
(params: { key: string; value: string }) => { ok: true }
```

### `secrets.delete`

Removes a secret from the plugin's encrypted secrets file.

```ts
(params: { key: string }) => { ok: true }
```

### `secrets.protection`

How secrets are protected at rest: `os-keyring`, or `unavailable` (no OS key store, or Linux `basic_text`), where `secrets.set` fails.

```ts
(params?: {}) => { status: "os-keyring" | "unavailable" }
```

### `settings.get`

Reads every setting the plugin owns.

```ts
(params?: {}) => { settings: Record<string, JSON> }
```

### `settings.set`

Writes one setting the plugin owns.

```ts
(params: { key: string; value: JSON }) => { ok: true }
```

### `shell.openExternal`

Opens an http:, https: or mailto: URL in the default browser. Needs a click or key press in the frame; desktop app only. Orca asks the person before an http(s) host the plugin was not allowed; `opened` is false if they cancel.

```ts
(params: { url: string }) => { opened: boolean; reason?: "cancelled" | "consent-unavailable" }
```

### `files.saveAs`

Offers data (a string or ArrayBuffer, up to 64 MiB) in Orca's save dialog; the plugin never learns the path. Needs a click or key press in the frame; desktop app only.

```ts
(params: { suggestedName?: string; mimeType?: string; data: string | ArrayBuffer }) => { status: "saved" | "cancelled" }
```

### `plugin.request`

Asks the plugin's own worker to run the handler it registered with `orca.panels.handle(name)`, starting the worker if needed; resolves with what the handler returned. `unknown_method` when no handler has that name.

```ts
(params: { name: string; input?: JSON; timeoutMs?: number }) => { output: JSON }
```

### `agents.list`

The agents in the focused workspace: their terminal, title, agent kind and status. `agent.status.changed` reports each change after.

```ts
(params?: {}) => { agents: { terminalId: string | null; title: string | null; agent: string | null; state: "working" | "blocked" | "waiting" | "done"; stateStartedAt: number }[] }
```

### `events.subscribe`

Delivers a workspace, agent or editor event to this panel as `orca.on(event)`; needs the event's read capability, when it has one. The frame APIs call it for you.

```ts
(params: { event: "workspace.created" | "workspace.removed" | "agent.status.changed" | "workspace.changed" | "editor.typography.changed" }) => { ok: true }
```

### `statusBar.update`

Changes one of the plugin's `contributes.statusBarItems` (named by `id`): fields given replace their current value, `visible: false` hides it. Desktop app only; lasts until Orca restarts, and is hidden while the plugin is disabled. A plugin with `main` and status bar items has its worker started when it is enabled and kept running while it stays enabled, so a worker can poll and update its items without an event or a hook.

```ts
(params: { id: string; text?: string; icon?: "activity" | "bar-chart-3" | "bell" | "blocks" | "book" | "bot" | "bug" | "calendar" | "cloud" | "code" | "database" | "file-text" | "flag" | "folder" | "gauge" | "globe" | "hammer" | "layers" | "lightbulb" | "package" | "plug" | "puzzle" | "rocket" | "star" | "terminal" | "wrench" | "zap" | "add" | "remove" | "delete" | "edit" | "refresh" | "search" | "settings" | "check" | "close" | "info" | "warning" | "error" | "open-external" | "copy" | "download" | "upload" | "play" | "pause" | "stop" | "more" | "expand" | "collapse" | "next" | "filter" | "branch" | "file" | "agent" | "link"; tone?: "neutral" | "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"; tooltip?: string; visible?: boolean }) => { ok: true }
```

### `appearance.read`

Reads the current desktop appearance revision for a conditional update.

```ts
(params?: {}) => { revision: string }
```

### `appearance.apply`

Publishes owned app/editor and terminal colors and selects them in the desktop. Returns publication, not renderer acknowledgement.

```ts
(params: { expectedRevision: string; app: string; terminal: string }) => { revision: string; themeId: string; mode: "dark" | "light"; delivery: "published" }
```

### `workspace.list`

Lists every workspace, Git worktrees and folders, on every host Orca reaches.

```ts
(params?: {}) => { workspaces: { id: string; kind: "worktree" | "folder"; name: string; project?: string | null; path: string; branch: string | null; hostId: string | null }[]; truncated: boolean }
```

### `workspace.open`

Shows a workspace in Orca, as clicking it in the sidebar does; a folder workspace needs the desktop app.

```ts
(params: { workspaceId: string }) => { opened: true }
```

### `workspace.rename`

Renames a workspace in Orca's sidebar, as renaming it by hand does; the name stays until it is renamed again.

```ts
(params: { workspaceId: string; name: string }) => { name: string }
```

### `terminal.create`

Opens a terminal in a workspace, optionally running a command, in the background.

```ts
(params: { workspaceId: string; title?: string; command?: string }) => { terminalId: string }
```

### `terminal.read`

Reads a terminal's newest output as plain text, at most 2000 lines.

```ts
(params: { terminalId: string; maxLines?: number }) => { lines: string[]; truncated: boolean }
```

### `agent.launch`

Starts an agent's CLI in a new terminal of a workspace, in the background, and returns as soon as it starts; a `prompt` is sent once the agent is ready.

```ts
(params: { workspaceId: string; agent: string; prompt?: string }) => { terminalId: string }
```

### `editor.open`

Opens a file of a workspace in an editor tab of Orca's window; desktop app only. `workspace.open` shows the workspace.

```ts
(params: { workspaceId: string; path: string }) => { opened: true }
```

### `commands.run`

Runs one of Orca's built-in actions in its window, never a plugin's replacement of it; desktop app only.

```ts
(params: { action: "worktree.history.back" | "worktree.history.forward" | "sidebar.left.toggle" | "sidebar.sleepingWorkspaces.toggle" | "floatingWorkspace.maximize" | "tab.rename" | "workspace.rename" | "workspace.openBoard" | "view.tasks" | "sidebar.right.toggle" | "sidebar.explorer.toggle" | "sidebar.search.toggle" | "sidebar.sourceControl.toggle" | "sidebar.checks.toggle" | "sidebar.ports.toggle" }) => { ran: true }
```

### `editor.readTypography`

The font family, size, weight, line height, ligatures, word wrap and minimap Orca's file editor uses now, editor zoom included. `editor.typography.changed` reports each change after.

```ts
(params?: {}) => { fontFamily: string; cssFontFamily: string; fontSize: number; fontWeight: string; lineHeight: number; fontLigatures: boolean; wordWrap: "on" | "off"; minimap: boolean }
```

## Events

A worker receives the events its manifest lists in `contributes.events` through `orca.events.on(event, handler)`, which returns `{ dispose() }`. Each needs `main`, the `trusted-worker` profile and its domain's capability (`workspace:read` or `agent:read`; editor events need none). `orca plugin types` writes the payloads as `PluginEvents` in `orca/host`.

| Event | Payload | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace.created` | `{ workspaceId: string; kind: "worktree" \| "folder"; path: string; branch: string }` | A worktree workspace was created. |
| `workspace.removed` | `{ workspaceId: string; kind: "worktree" \| "folder"; path: string }` | A worktree workspace was removed. |
| `agent.status.changed` | `{ workspaceId: string \| null; paneKey: string; terminalId?: string; title?: string; state: "working" \| "blocked" \| "waiting" \| "done"; receivedAt: number; mainAgent?: { state: "working" \| "blocked" \| "waiting" \| "done"; outcome?: "success" \| "failure" \| "cancellation" \| "superseded" \| "interruption" \| "unconfirmed"; stateStartedAt: number } }` | An agent in a terminal pane changed status; `workspaceId` is null when Orca cannot tie the pane to a workspace, and `terminalId` names its terminal when Orca lists it. |
| `workspace.changed` | `{ context: { branch: string; displayName: string; terminals: { id: string; title?: string }[] } \| null }` | The focused workspace changed, or its terminals were opened, closed or renamed; `context` is what `workspace.readContext` now answers. Each new subscriber first gets the current context. |
| `editor.typography.changed` | `{ fontFamily: string; cssFontFamily: string; fontSize: number; fontWeight: string; lineHeight: number; fontLigatures: boolean; wordWrap: "on" \| "off"; minimap: boolean }` | What Orca's file editor uses changed (a setting or the editor zoom); the payload is what `editor.readTypography` now answers. Needs no capability. |

## Hooks

A worker changes or stops what Orca is about to do with `orca.hooks.on(hook, (event, next) => ...)`, which returns `{ dispose() }`. Each hook must be listed in `contributes.hooks` (`main` and the `trusted-worker` profile; no capability). Return `next(event)` to go on, with the fields the hook allows changed; return a result such as `{ deny: reason }` to stop; return nothing to pass. Plugins run one after another (installed plugins by key, then development folders), then Orca acts on what is left. Orca starts the workers of plugins that list hooks (or status bar items) as soon as they are enabled and keeps them running until they are disabled. A handler that takes longer than 2 s, a worker that does not start within the worker ready timeout, a throw, a crash or a disabled plugin counts as having passed, and `orca plugin logs` shows the hook, the plugin and how long it took. A guard that must fail closed sets `"onError": "deny"` on its `contributes.hooks` entry; then those failures refuse the action, naming the plugin. Decide before any other awaited call: an awaited host call ahead of your `{ deny }` can fail or time out and let the action through.

Hooks run in the workers of the Orca that handles the request, before it acts: for an SSH or WSL terminal or workspace, that is the desktop, before the work is sent to its host. A paired client reaching a remote Orca server is decided by that server's plugins. `orca plugin types` writes the events as `PluginHooks` in `orca/host`; `orca/testing` `mountWorker(...).hooks.fire(hook, event)` returns what the chain decided.

| Hook | Event | Stop result | `next` may change | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `terminal.send` | `{ terminalId: string; text: string; enter: boolean; inputKind: "driving" \| "orchestration" \| "launch" }` | `{ deny: string }` | `text`, `enter` | Text Orca, the CLI or a plugin is about to send to a terminal. A person typing (on the desktop, a phone or a paired client) is never hooked, and prompts Orca submits to an agent take `agent.prompt.before` instead. Writes to one terminal stay in order while a hook decides. Rewrite `text` or `enter` with `next`, or return `{ deny }` to refuse the send. |
| `workspace.create.before` | `{ kind: "worktree" \| "folder"; projectId: string; name: string; branch?: string; base?: string }` | `{ deny: string }` | `name`, `branch`, `base` | A worktree or folder workspace is about to be created. Change `name`, `branch` or `base` with `next`, or return `{ deny }` to refuse it. |
| `workspace.create.after` | `{ workspaceId: string; kind: "worktree" \| "folder"; path: string; branch: string }` | none | nothing | A worktree or folder workspace was created. Observe only: Orca does not wait for it, and results are ignored. |
| `agent.launch.before` | `{ agent: string; workspaceId: string \| null; workspaceKind: "worktree" \| "folder" \| null; terminalId?: string; command: string; env: Record<string, string> }` | `{ deny: string }` | `command`, `env` | Orca is about to start an agent CLI in a terminal, from any launcher (new tab, workspace create, CLI, automation, orchestration). Change `command` or add `env` with `next`, or return `{ deny }` to refuse the launch. Restores of saved sessions are not hooked. |
| `agent.prompt.before` | `{ agent: string \| null; terminalId: string; prompt: string; inputKind: "driving" \| "orchestration" \| "launch" }` | `{ deny: string }` | `prompt` | Orca is about to submit a prompt to an agent in a terminal: a launch prompt, an orchestration dispatch, an issue or task prompt, or `orca terminal send` to an agent. A prompt a person submits is never hooked, and writes to one terminal stay in order while it decides. Rewrite `prompt` with `next`, or return `{ deny }` to refuse it. |
| `agent.tool.before` | `{ agent: string; workspaceId: string \| null; terminalId?: string; tool: string; input: JSON; callId?: string }` | `{ deny: string }` | `input` | An agent in an Orca terminal is about to run a tool. Claude Code waits for the answer: return `{ deny }` to refuse the call (the agent sees the reason) or change `input` with `next`; the person is still asked as usual. Other agents only report the call, so their results are ignored. Agents on SSH or WSL hosts are not hooked yet. |
| `agent.tool.after` | `{ agent: string; workspaceId: string \| null; terminalId?: string; tool: string; input: JSON; callId?: string; output?: JSON }` | none | nothing | An agent in an Orca terminal finished a tool call (successfully or not). Observe only: Orca does not wait for it. |
| `editor.save.before` | `{ workspaceId: string \| null; path: string; languageId?: string; text: string }` | `{ deny: string }` | `text` | The person is about to save a text file from an Orca editor tab (an explicit save, not autosave). Change `text` with `next` (format on save) or return `{ deny }` to refuse the save, which shows your reason. Edits made while the hook ran stay unsaved. |

## Errors

A failed call rejects with an `Error` carrying `code`, `message`, `retryable` and, for `rate_limited`, `retryAfterMs`. Treat a code not listed here as `action_failed`:

- `invalid_request`: the call itself is malformed.
- `invalid_params`: params do not match the method, including a field this Orca does not know; the message names it.
- `unknown_method`: the method does not exist in this Orca.
- `capability_denied`: the manifest does not declare the capability.
- `consent_required`: the plugin is disabled or the user has not approved this version.
- `not_permitted`: the method or document is not available here, e.g. a worker-only method from a panel.
- `rate_limited`: calls arrive faster than the budget; `retryAfterMs` says when to try again.
- `unavailable`: the service behind the method is not running yet.
- `action_failed`: the method ran and failed.
- `cancelled`: the caller aborted the call through its `signal`.
- `timeout`: Orca gave up waiting.
- `conflict`: the call was made against a stale version, e.g. an editor edit after an outside change.
- `too_large`: the message is larger than Orca accepts.

## Stability and deprecation

Plugins are in Alpha: the manifest v2 format and catalog format are stable contracts; items listed as experimental in [Plugin authoring](./plugin-authoring.md#stability) may change.

- **Host API 1 is frozen.** Within `pluginApi` 1, methods, params and results only grow: a new method or a new optional param arrives with a higher `Since` minor, and nothing listed here is removed, renamed or narrowed.
- **Deprecation.** A method to be retired is marked deprecated in this table and keeps working for the rest of the major.
- **New majors.** A breaking change ships as a new `pluginApi` major beside the old one. Orca refuses a manifest whose `pluginApi` names a major it does not implement, with "update Orca", instead of loading it against the wrong API.
- **Detect, do not assume.** Check `orca.host.has(name)` or `orca.api.minor` before calling a method newer than the oldest Orca you support; a call that slips through fails with `unknown_method`.
